title: The Algorithm Is Not the Behavior: Learned Priors Override Look-Ahead in a Chess-Playing Neural Network
abstract: arXiv:2508.21380v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Recent mechanistic work has uncovered learned algorithms within neural networks, from modular arithmetic to search and planning in game-playing agents. But does algorithmic structure guarantee algorithmic behavior? We investigate this in Leela Chess Zero, the strongest neural chess engine, where prior work identified learned look-ahead. By extending the logit lens to its move-selecting policy network, we discover that correct puzzle solutions--including immediate checkmates--often appear in intermediate layers but are systematically overridden in the final output, a phenomenon we term "forgotten puzzles". Replicating prior analyses on these positions, we find that look-ahead operates normally--future moves of the correct continuation are represented, causally important, and linearly decodable--ruling out a failure of the algorithm. translated_title: 算法并非行为：习得先验在国际象棋神经网络中覆盖前瞻机制
translated_abstract: 近期的机制可解释性研究揭示了神经网络内部习得的算法，从模运算到博弈智能体中的搜索与规划。但算法结构是否必然保证算法行为？我们在 Leela Chess Zero——最强的神经国际象棋引擎中研究了这一问题，此前的工作已在其内部识别出习得的前瞻（look-ahead）机制。通过将 logit lens 方法扩展到其选择走子的策略网络，我们发现正确的谜题解答——包括一步将杀——经常出现在中间层中，却在最终输出中被系统性地覆盖，我们将这一现象称为“被遗忘的谜题”（forgotten puzzles）。在这些局面上复制先前的分析后，我们发现前瞻机制运行正常——正确续着的后续走法被表示出来、具有因果重要性、且可线性解码——从而排除了算法失效的可能性。相反，靠后的层越来越倾向于安全保守而非激进的下法。为了检验这种偏移……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究发现即使 Leela Chess Zero 内部的前瞻搜索算法运行正常，靠后层的习得保守先验仍会系统性覆盖中间层已出现的正确解法（“被遗忘的谜题”），证明算法结构并不保证算法行为。
en_tdlr: In Leela Chess Zero, look-ahead operates normally in intermediate layers, but learned priors in late layers favoring safe play systematically override correct solutions—showing that algorithmic structure does not guarantee algorithmic behavior.
